questions.text: Which case is used for the subject of a Latin sentence?

feedback: The accusative is mainly for the direct object

questions.solution: The subject (the person or thing doing the action) is in the nominative
questions.hint: Think of the case you find a noun in when you look it up in the dictionary

questions.text: Which case is used for the direct object of a Latin verb? Give the case in English.
questions.solution: The direct object is in the accusative, e.g. canem in «puella canem videt»
questions.hint: In «puella canem videt», it is the case of canem

questions.text: What does «puella» mean?
questions.solution: puella = girl; puer = boy; femina = woman; mater = mother
questions.hint: It is a first declension noun for a young person

questions.text: Which case shows possession, translated with 'of'? Give the case in English.
questions.solution: The genitive shows possession: domini = of the master
questions.hint: In «filius regis» (the son of the king), it is the case of regis

questions.text: Which declension does «amicus, amici» (friend) belong to?

feedback: First declension nouns have genitive -ae, like puella, puellae

questions.solution: Nouns with nominative -us and genitive -i are second declension
questions.hint: Look at the genitive singular ending -i

questions.text: Give the accusative singular of «puella». Type the Latin word.

feedback.puellae: puellae is genitive/dative singular or nominative plural

questions.solution: First declension accusative singular ends in -am: puella → puellam
questions.hint: First declension nouns add -m in the accusative singular

questions.text: What is the nominative plural of «puella»?

feedback: puellas is the accusative plural
puellis is the dative or ablative plural

questions.solution: First declension nominative plural ends in -ae: puellae
questions.hint: The ending is the same as the genitive singular

questions.text: In «puer dominum videt», which word is the subject?

feedback: dominum ends in -um: it is accusative, the object
videt is the verb

questions.solution: puer is nominative, so it is the subject: the boy sees the master
questions.hint: Look for the noun in the nominative case

questions.text: What case is «templo» in the phrase «in templo»? Give the case in English.

feedback.accusative: in + accusative means 'into'; here it means 'in'

questions.solution: in meaning 'in' or 'on' takes the ablative: in templo = in the temple
questions.hint: in meaning 'in' (place where, not motion into) takes this case

questions.text: Give the genitive singular of «dominus». Type the Latin word.
questions.solution: Second declension genitive singular ends in -i: domini = of the master
questions.hint: dominus is second declension, like amicus, amici

questions.text: What does the preposition «ad» mean, followed by the accusative?

feedback: 'from' is a or ab
'with' is cum
'out of' is e or ex

questions.solution: ad + accusative = to, towards: ad urbem = to the city
questions.hint: It shows movement in a direction

questions.text: What does the preposition «cum» mean, as in «cum amicis»? Answer in English.
questions.solution: cum + ablative = with: cum amicis = with friends
questions.hint: Think of a word that links you to your companions

questions.text: Translate: «puer puellam videt».

feedback: puellam is accusative, so the girl is the one being seen

questions.solution: puer (nominative) is the subject, puellam (accusative) the object, videt is present: the boy sees the girl
questions.hint: Find the nominative first; the -am ending marks the object

questions.text: Which form of «magnus» agrees with «templum» (nominative singular)?
questions.solution: templum is neuter, so the neuter nominative magnum agrees: templum magnum
questions.hint: What gender is templum?

questions.text: Translate «cum amicis». Answer in English.
questions.solution: cum + ablative plural: cum amicis = with (his/her) friends
questions.hint: amicis is the ablative plural of amicus

questions.text: Give the dative plural of «puella». Type the Latin word.
questions.solution: First declension dative and ablative plural end in -is: puellis
questions.hint: The dative plural and ablative plural share the same ending

questions.text: What does «e foro» mean?
questions.solution: e/ex + ablative = out of: e foro = out of the forum
questions.hint: e is a short form of ex

questions.text: Translate «in villa». Answer in English.
questions.solution: in + ablative = in: in villa = in the villa (house)
questions.hint: villa is ablative here, so in shows place where

questions.text: In «canis cibum puero dat», what is the case of «puero»?

feedback: The form puero can be ablative, but here it means 'to the boy'

questions.solution: The dog gives food to the boy: puero is the indirect object, so dative (the form is the same as the ablative)
questions.hint: Ask: to whom is the food given?

questions.text: Translate: «amici dominum in foro viderunt».

options: The friends see the master in the forum
The friends saw the master in the forum
The friend saw the master in the forum
The master saw the friends in the forum

questions.solution: amici (nominative plural) + viderunt (perfect plural): the friends saw the master in the forum
questions.hint: Check the verb ending: -erunt is perfect plural

questions.text: In «nomen regis erat Tarquinius», what does «regis» mean? Answer in English.
questions.solution: regis is the genitive of rex: the name of the king was Tarquinius
questions.hint: rex, regis: the -is ending is genitive singular

questions.text: Give the accusative plural of «dominus». Type the Latin word.
questions.solution: Second declension accusative plural ends in -os: dominos
questions.hint: dominus is second declension; the masculine accusative plural ends in -s

questions.text: Which phrase means 'the brave soldiers' (nominative)?

feedback: militum fortium is genitive plural
fortis is not nominative plural; the adjective must be fortes

questions.solution: miles is third declension (nominative plural milites); fortis agrees: milites fortes
questions.hint: Both words must be nominative plural

questions.text: In «Marcus librum amici legit», what case is «amici»? Give the case in English.
questions.solution: Marcus is the subject, so amici means 'of the friend': genitive singular
questions.hint: Marcus is already the subject, so amici cannot be nominative plural here

questions.text: Which is the correct translation of «Romani urbem magnis muris defenderunt»?

options: The Romans defended the great walls of the city
The city defended the Romans with great walls
The Romans are defending the city with great walls
The Romans defended the city with great walls

questions.solution: magnis muris is ablative (means): with great walls; defenderunt is perfect
questions.hint: Work out the case of magnis muris and the tense of defenderunt

questions.text: In «femina, quam heri vidi, Romam venit», what does «quam» refer to?
questions.solution: quam is a feminine relative pronoun referring to femina: the woman, whom I saw yesterday, came to Rome
questions.hint: A relative pronoun refers back to a noun that comes before it

questions.text: Why is «Roma» in the ablative in «Roma discessit», with no preposition?

options: Names of cities use the ablative alone to mean 'from'
Roma is the subject of the sentence

questions.solution: With names of cities, the ablative alone means 'from': Roma discessit = he left Rome
questions.hint: discessit means 'he/she departed'

questions.text: Translate «in urbem» (in + accusative). Answer in English.

feedback.in the city: That would be in urbe (ablative); the accusative shows motion

questions.solution: in + accusative shows motion: in urbem = into the city
questions.hint: in + accusative is different from in + ablative

questions.text: Give the ablative plural of «miles» (soldier). Type the Latin word.
questions.solution: miles, militis is third declension: ablative plural militibus
questions.hint: Find the stem from the genitive militis, then add the third declension ending

questions.text: In «rex, vir magnae virtutis, hostes vicit», what does «magnae virtutis» mean? Answer in English.
questions.solution: Genitive of description: vir magnae virtutis = a man of great courage
questions.hint: Both words are genitive singular and describe vir

questions.text: What does «amat» mean?
questions.solution: The ending -t means he/she/it: amat = he (she) loves
questions.hint: Look at the personal ending of the verb

questions.text: What does the personal ending «-mus» show about who is doing the action? Answer in English.
questions.solution: -mus = we, e.g. portamus = we carry
questions.hint: Compare portamus with porto (I carry)

questions.text: Which is the infinitive of «porto» (I carry)?
questions.solution: First conjugation infinitives end in -are: portare = to carry
questions.hint: Infinitives mean 'to …'

questions.text: What does the personal ending «-nt» show about who is doing the action? Answer in English.
questions.solution: -nt = they, e.g. portant = they carry
questions.hint: Compare portant with portat (he carries)

questions.text: What does «sum» mean?
questions.solution: sum = I am (from esse, to be)
questions.hint: It is the first person of esse

questions.text: Give the Latin for 'he is'. Type one word.
questions.solution: est = he/she/it is (from esse)
questions.hint: It is the third person singular of esse

questions.text: Which tense is «portabat»?
questions.solution: -ba- marks the imperfect: portabat = he was carrying
questions.hint: Look for the tense sign -ba-

questions.text: Which tense is «portavit»?

feedback: The pluperfect would be portaverat

questions.solution: portavit uses the perfect stem portav- with -it: he carried
questions.hint: Look at the -v- before the ending: it marks a different stem from the present

questions.text: Translate «portabant». Answer in English.
questions.solution: -ba- = imperfect, -nt = they: they were carrying
questions.hint: -ba- marks the imperfect tense; then look at the person ending

questions.text: Give the Latin for 'they are'. Type one word.
questions.solution: sunt = they are (from esse)
questions.hint: It is the third person plural of esse

questions.text: Which form is the imperative ('carry!') addressed to one person?

feedback: portate is the plural command

questions.solution: The singular imperative is the stem: porta! (portate! is plural)
questions.hint: Take the infinitive and remove -re

questions.text: Translate «dormiebat». Answer in English.
questions.solution: dormio = I sleep; -ieba- is imperfect: he was sleeping
questions.hint: dormitory comes from this verb

questions.text: Translate: «puellae cantabant».
questions.solution: puellae (nominative plural) + cantabant (imperfect, they): the girls were singing
questions.hint: The verb ending tells you whether the subject is singular or plural

questions.text: Which form means 'we had carried'?
questions.solution: The pluperfect adds -eram- to the perfect stem: portaveramus
questions.hint: 'had …' is the pluperfect

questions.text: What tense is «laudaverat»? Give the tense in English.

feedback.perfect: The perfect would be laudavit; -era- shows 'had'

questions.solution: Perfect stem laudav- + -erat: he had praised (pluperfect)
questions.hint: Look at the -era- after the perfect stem

questions.text: Give the third person plural perfect of «porto» ('they carried'). Type the Latin word.
questions.solution: Perfect stem portav- + -erunt: portaverunt
questions.hint: Find the perfect stem, then add the 'they' ending of the perfect

questions.text: What does «ire» mean?
questions.solution: ire = to go (eo, ire, ii); esse = to be; velle = to want; posse = to be able
questions.hint: Think of English 'exit' (he goes out)

questions.text: Translate «possumus». Answer in English.
questions.solution: possum, posse = to be able: possumus = we can
questions.hint: It is a form of possum; the ending -mus means 'we'

questions.text: Translate: «milites, ubi hostes viderunt, fugerunt».

options: The soldiers saw the enemy and are fleeing
When the soldiers saw the enemy, they fled
The soldiers fled before they saw the enemy
When the enemy saw the soldiers, they fled

questions.solution: ubi = when; hostes is accusative here; fugerunt = they fled
questions.hint: ubi + perfect means 'when'

questions.text: Which verb form is passive?
questions.solution: The passive ending -tur means 'is being …': portatur = he/it is carried
questions.hint: Passive endings include -r, -ris, -tur

questions.text: Translate «portantur». Answer in English.

feedback.they carry: That would be portant; -ntur makes it passive

questions.solution: -ntur is the present passive 'they' ending: portantur = they are (being) carried
questions.hint: -ntur is a passive ending

questions.text: Give the imperfect 'I was carrying' of «porto». Type the Latin word.
questions.solution: Stem porta- + -ba- + -m: portabam
questions.hint: The imperfect tense sign is -ba-

questions.text: In «dux milites pugnare iussit», what does «pugnare» mean?
questions.solution: iubeo + accusative + infinitive: the leader ordered the soldiers to fight
questions.hint: pugnare ends in -are

questions.text: Translate «voluit». Answer in English.
questions.solution: volo, velle, volui: voluit = he wanted
questions.hint: volo means 'I want'; -it on a perfect stem is the perfect

questions.text: Which is the correct translation of «hostes, a militibus victi, fugerunt»?

options: The enemy, defeated by the soldiers, fled
The enemy defeated the soldiers and fled
The soldiers, defeated by the enemy, fled
The enemy fled before they defeated the soldiers

questions.solution: victi is a perfect passive participle agreeing with hostes; a militibus = by the soldiers
questions.hint: victi is a perfect passive participle: 'having been …'

questions.text: In «puer, cibum consumens, risit», what does «consumens» mean?

feedback: 'having eaten' would be a perfect participle

questions.solution: -ns is a present participle: consumens = eating
questions.hint: Participles ending in -ns are present participles

questions.text: Which sentence is passive?
questions.solution: capta est is perfect passive: the city was captured by the Romans
questions.hint: Look for est or sunt with a participle

questions.text: Translate «ab hostibus capti sunt». Answer in English.

accept: they were captured by the enemy
they were taken by the enemy
they have been captured by the enemy
they were caught by the enemy
they have been taken by the enemy
they were captured by the enemies
they were taken by the enemies
they have been captured by the enemies

questions.solution: capti sunt = they were captured (perfect passive); ab hostibus = by the enemy
questions.hint: ab + ablative with a passive verb means 'by'

questions.text: Give the third person singular perfect of «eo» ('he went'). Type the Latin word.

feedback.it: That form is the present tense (he goes)
feedback.ibat: ibat is the imperfect (he was going)

questions.solution: eo, ire, ii (or ivi): iit (or ivit) = he went
questions.hint: eo is irregular; its perfect is ii or ivi

questions.text: In «cras Romam ibimus», what tense is «ibimus»? Give the tense in English.
questions.solution: cras = tomorrow; ibimus = we shall go (future of eo)
questions.hint: cras means 'tomorrow'

questions.text: What does «aqua» mean?
questions.solution: aqua = water (English 'aquarium')
questions.hint: Think of the English word 'aquatic'

questions.text: What does «rex» mean? Answer in English.
questions.solution: rex, regis = king (English 'regal')
questions.hint: Think of the English word 'regal'

questions.text: What does «bellum» mean?
questions.solution: bellum = war; bellus = pretty; pax = peace
questions.hint: Think of the English word 'belligerent'

questions.text: What does «mater» mean? Answer in English.
questions.solution: mater = mother; pater = father
questions.hint: Think of the English word 'maternal'

questions.text: What does «urbs» mean?
questions.solution: urbs = city (English 'urban'); via = road; murus = wall; domus = house
questions.hint: Think of the English word 'urban'

questions.text: What does «magnus» mean? Answer in English.
questions.solution: magnus = big, great (English 'magnify')
questions.hint: Think of the English word 'magnify'

questions.text: What does «iter» mean?

feedback: 'again' is iterum

questions.solution: iter = journey; iterum = again; hostis = enemy; cibus = food
questions.hint: Think of the English word 'itinerary'

questions.text: Which Latin word means 'often'?
questions.solution: saepe = often; semper = always; numquam = never; iam = now, already
questions.hint: Rule out the words you know: semper means 'always' and numquam means 'never'

questions.text: What does «semper» mean? Answer in English.
questions.solution: semper = always; numquam = never
questions.hint: The US Marines' motto is 'Semper fidelis'

questions.text: What does «tamen» mean? Answer in English.
questions.solution: tamen = however, nevertheless
questions.hint: It introduces a contrast, often as the second word of a sentence

questions.text: What does «hostis» mean?

feedback: This is a false friend: the English 'host' is not the meaning

questions.solution: hostis = enemy (English 'hostile'); miles = soldier
questions.hint: Think of the English word 'hostile'

questions.text: Give the Latin word for 'and'. Type one word.
questions.solution: et = and (also atque or ac)
questions.hint: The ending -que on a word has the same meaning; the separate word has two letters

questions.text: Which English word comes from «aqua» (water)?
questions.solution: An aquarium is a tank of water
questions.hint: Which word is about a container of water?

questions.text: Which English word comes from «navis» (ship)?
questions.solution: The navy is a fleet of ships
questions.hint: Which word is connected with ships?

questions.text: The English word 'pedestrian' comes from «pes, pedis». What does «pes» mean? Answer in English.
questions.solution: pes, pedis = foot: a pedestrian travels on foot
questions.hint: A pedestrian is someone who walks

questions.text: Translate «puer laetus est». Answer in English.
questions.solution: puer = boy; laetus = happy; est = is
questions.hint: laetus describes a feeling

questions.text: What does «timeo» mean?
questions.solution: timeo = I fear (English 'timid'); teneo = I hold; video = I see; audio = I hear
questions.hint: Think of the English word 'timid'

questions.text: Give the Latin word for 'I see'. Type the Latin word.
questions.solution: video = I see (videre = to see)
questions.hint: Start from videre (to see) and give the 'I' form of the present tense

questions.text: Translate: «nuntius ad urbem celeriter cucurrit».

options: The messenger is running quickly to the city
The messenger ran quickly to the city
The messenger walked slowly to the city
The messengers ran quickly from the city

questions.solution: nuntius = messenger; celeriter = quickly; cucurrit = he ran (perfect of curro)
questions.hint: cucurrit is the perfect of curro (I run)

questions.text: Translate: «mercator multam pecuniam habebat».

options: The merchants had a lot of money
The merchant had a lot of money
The merchant has a lot of money

questions.solution: mercator = merchant; multam pecuniam = much money; habebat = he had (imperfect)
questions.hint: habebat is imperfect, and mercator is singular

questions.text: Translate «senex filium vocavit». Answer in English.

accept: the old man called his son
the old man called the son
the old man called a son
the old man summoned his son
the old man called for his son
the old man called to his son
the old man summoned the son

questions.solution: senex = old man; filium = son (accusative); vocavit = called (perfect)
questions.hint: senex means 'old man' (English 'senior')

questions.text: The English word 'audience' comes from «audio». What does «audio» mean? Answer in English.
questions.solution: audio = I hear, I listen to; an audience listens
questions.hint: An audience is a group of people who …?

questions.text: Which English word comes from «scribo» (I write)?
questions.solution: A script is something written
questions.hint: Which word is about writing?

questions.text: Give the Latin for 'the boys' (nominative plural). Type one word.
questions.solution: puer, pueri (second declension): nominative plural pueri
questions.hint: puer is second declension like amicus; masculine nominative plural ends in -i

questions.text: Which is the correct translation of «Romani, quamquam fessi erant, fortiter pugnaverunt»?

options: Although the Romans were tired, they fought bravely
The Romans were tired and so they did not fight
The Romans fought bravely and then became tired
The Romans were tired, so they fought badly

questions.solution: quamquam = although; fessi = tired; fortiter = bravely; pugnaverunt = they fought
questions.hint: quamquam introduces a contrast

questions.text: In «postquam cenam consumpserunt, dormiverunt», what happened first?
questions.solution: postquam = after: after they had eaten dinner, they slept
questions.hint: postquam means 'after'

questions.text: Translate: «nemo cives servare poterat».

options: No one wanted to save the citizens
Nobody is able to save the citizens
No one was able to save the citizens
The citizens could save no one

questions.solution: nemo = no one (subject); cives = citizens (accusative); poterat = was able
questions.hint: nemo is the subject; poterat is imperfect

questions.text: Translate «non diu manebant». Answer in English.

accept: they did not stay for long
they did not stay for a long time
they didn't stay for a long time
they were not staying for long
they did not remain for long

questions.solution: non = not; diu = for a long time; manebant = they stayed (imperfect)
questions.hint: diu means 'for a long time'; manebant comes from maneo

questions.text: «dux milites hortatus est ut fortiter pugnarent.» What did the leader encourage the soldiers to do? Answer in English.
questions.solution: ut + subjunctive gives the content of the encouragement: to fight bravely
questions.hint: fortiter is an adverb from fortis (brave)

questions.text: Give the Latin word for 'never'. Type the Latin word.
questions.solution: numquam = never; semper = always; saepe = often
questions.hint: It is the opposite of semper

questions.text: What was the head of a Roman family called?
questions.solution: The paterfamilias was the oldest male, who had authority over the whole household
questions.hint: The name contains the Latin word for 'father'

questions.text: Who was the Roman king of the gods? Give his Roman name.

feedback.Zeus: Zeus is his Greek name; give the Roman name

questions.solution: Jupiter was king of the gods (the Greek Zeus)
questions.hint: He is the Roman version of the Greek Zeus

questions.text: What was the main public square and meeting place of a Roman town called?
questions.solution: The forum was the centre of public, business and political life
questions.hint: Today the word is used for a place of public discussion

questions.text: In Roman legend, which animal fed the twins Romulus and Remus? Answer in English.
questions.solution: A she-wolf fed the twins by the River Tiber
questions.hint: It is a wild animal related to the dog

questions.text: Who was the Roman goddess of love?
questions.solution: Venus was the goddess of love (the Greek Aphrodite)
questions.hint: A planet is named after her

questions.text: What was the Latin name for the Roman province of Britain? Give the Latin name.
questions.solution: The Romans called the province Britannia
questions.hint: The name appears on old British coins next to a seated female figure

questions.text: Who was the Roman god of war?
questions.solution: Mars was the god of war (the Greek Ares); the month of March is named after him
questions.hint: The month of March is named after him

questions.text: What was a Roman legion?
questions.solution: A legion was a large army unit of about 5,000 soldiers
questions.hint: It was part of the Roman army

questions.text: What was the officer called who commanded a century (about 80 men) in the Roman army? Give the term.
questions.solution: A centurion commanded a century of about 80 men
questions.hint: The title comes from the word for the unit he led

questions.text: Which Roman god of the sea was the same as the Greek Poseidon? Give his Roman name.
questions.solution: Neptune was the Roman god of the sea
questions.hint: A planet far from the Sun is named after him

questions.text: What was the atrium in a Roman house?

options: The main hall, often with an opening in the roof

questions.solution: The atrium was the main hall; rain fell through the compluvium into the impluvium pool
questions.hint: It was the first large room a visitor entered

questions.text: What was the hot room in Roman baths called? Give the Latin term.

feedback.tepidarium: The tepidarium was the warm room
feedback.frigidarium: The frigidarium was the cold room

questions.solution: caldarium (also spelt calidarium) = hot room; tepidarium = warm room; frigidarium = cold room
questions.hint: The Latin word calidus means 'hot'

questions.text: Which emperor ordered a wall to be built across northern Britain in about AD 122?
questions.solution: Hadrian's Wall was begun in about AD 122
questions.hint: The wall is named after him

questions.text: Under which emperor did the Romans invade Britain in AD 43?

feedback: Caesar led expeditions in 55 and 54 BC, and he was never emperor

questions.solution: The invasion of AD 43 took place under Claudius
questions.hint: Julius Caesar visited Britain earlier but did not conquer it

questions.text: Which queen of the Iceni led a revolt against the Romans in AD 60–61? Give her name.
questions.solution: Boudicca led the Iceni revolt in AD 60–61
questions.hint: Her statue with a chariot stands near Westminster Bridge in London

questions.text: In Roman legend, Aeneas escaped from which city when it was destroyed by the Greeks? Give the city.
questions.solution: Aeneas escaped from burning Troy and later reached Italy
questions.hint: The Greeks used a wooden horse to capture it

questions.text: What were the lares in a Roman home?

options: Household gods who protected the family

questions.solution: The lares were household gods, honoured at a shrine called the lararium
questions.hint: They were worshipped at the lararium shrine

questions.text: What is the common name of the large amphitheatre in Rome where gladiators fought, opened in AD 80? Give its name.
questions.solution: The Colosseum (Flavian Amphitheatre) was opened in AD 80
questions.hint: Its name may come from a colossal statue that stood nearby

questions.text: According to a well-known version of the legend, why did Romulus kill Remus?

options: Remus refused to fight the Sabines
Remus jumped over the walls Romulus was building
Remus wanted to be king of Troy

questions.solution: In the best-known version, Remus mocked Romulus by leaping over his new walls
questions.hint: It happened while Romulus was founding his new city

questions.text: Roman boys from free families wore a bulla. What was it?

options: A toga with a purple stripe
A protective amulet worn around the neck
feedback: That is the toga praetexta, also worn by boys

questions.solution: The bulla was a protective amulet, dedicated to the household gods when a boy came of age
questions.hint: It was believed to keep the wearer safe

questions.text: What was a Roman soldier's short stabbing sword called? Give the Latin term.

feedback.pilum: The pilum was a throwing javelin

questions.solution: The gladius was a short stabbing sword (gladiator comes from the same word)
questions.hint: The word 'gladiator' comes from it

questions.text: Which Roman goddess of wisdom was the same as the Greek goddess Athena? Give her Roman name.
questions.solution: Minerva was the goddess of wisdom (the Greek Athena)
questions.hint: In Roman Bath she was linked with the local goddess Sulis

questions.text: What did a Roman haruspex do?

options: Taught boys to read and write
Examined the insides of sacrificed animals to read omens

questions.solution: A haruspex read the will of the gods from the organs of sacrificed animals
questions.hint: It was a religious role connected with sacrifice

questions.text: What was the Roman name of the town at modern Bath, famous for its hot springs? Give the Latin name.
questions.solution: Aquae Sulis = the waters of Sulis
questions.hint: The name means 'the waters of Sulis'; start with the Latin word for water

questions.text: Why were Roman army forts built to a standard plan?

options: Soldiers knew where everything was and could build them quickly
The emperor designed every fort personally
They had to look like Greek temples
Only one architect worked for the army

questions.solution: A standard layout let soldiers build forts fast and find their way in any fort
questions.hint: Think about soldiers who moved from one fort to another

questions.text: Which statement about the Vestal Virgins is accurate?

options: They tended the sacred fire of Vesta in Rome
They were the wives of Roman priests
They served for one year only

questions.solution: The Vestals kept the sacred fire of Vesta burning; they served for 30 years
questions.hint: Vesta was the goddess of the hearth

questions.text: Why was the Roman road network important for controlling Britain?

options: Roads were built mainly for chariot racing
It removed the need for an army
Troops and supplies could move quickly between forts and towns
It stopped the Britons from farming

questions.solution: Straight, paved roads let the army and supplies move quickly around the province
questions.hint: Think about what an army needs in order to react quickly

questions.text: In the Aeneid, Aeneas leaves Carthage and its queen to follow his destiny. Who was the queen? Give her name.
questions.solution: Dido, queen of Carthage, fell in love with Aeneas, who left her for Italy
questions.hint: She founded the city of Carthage in North Africa

questions.text: Which Roman leader was assassinated on the Ides of March, 44 BC? Give his name.
questions.solution: Julius Caesar was assassinated on 15 March 44 BC
questions.hint: The month of July is named after him

questions.text: Which Roman festival in December involved gift-giving, feasting and relaxed social rules? Give its name.
questions.solution: The Saturnalia was a December festival in honour of Saturn
questions.hint: It honoured the god Saturn
